sentences.text:
Author: K. Lakshman
Bench: K.Lakshman, P.Sree Sudha
 The Honourable Sri Justice K. Lakshman
 And
 The Honourable Smt. Justice P. Sree Sudha
 Writ Petition No.9739 of 2023
Order:

(Per Honourable Sri Justice K. Lakshman) Heard Ms.R. Sowmya Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner, and the learned Special Government Pleader, representing the learned Additional Advocate-General, for the respondents.

2. This Writ Petition is filed by the petitioner challenging the detention order passed by the 2nd respondent vide proceedings No.07/PD-CELL/CYB/2023, dated 28.01.2023 (for short, 'the impugned detention order') and the Confirmation Order passed by 1st respondent vide G.O.Rt.No.420, dated 17.03.2023, as illegal, arbitrary, improper, unilateral, unconstitutional and violative of Articles 21 and 22 of the Constitution of India, and to set forth the detenu free, viz.,
Mohammed Adnan.
3.
Petitioner herein is wife of the detenu.
KL,J & PSS,J

4. The impugned detention order was issued by the 2nd respondent on the ground that the detenu had involved in a criminal case, viz., Crime No.381 of 2022, for offences punishable under Section 363 and 302 of I.P.C. on the file of Mailardevpally Police Station, Cyberabad.
5. Perusal of the detention order dated 28.01.2023 would reveal that the same was passed by the 2nd respondent by relying solely on a solitary case referred above.
6. The allegation levelled against the detenu is that he had kidnapped another rowdy-sheeter and murdered him.

sentences.text: 7. The Investigation Officer had already completed investigation in the above crime and also laid charge-sheet, and the case is at pre-revision stage.

8. In the grounds accompanying the impugned detention order, the 2nd respondent referred to three criminal cases relating to the detenu during the years 2019 to 2021, viz., (i) Crime No.133/2019, for offences punishable under Section 352 of I.P.C. and Section 27 of Indian Arms Act,
1959, (ii) Crime No.307/2019, for offences punishable under Section 506 of I.P.C. and Section 27 of Indian Arms Act, 1959; and (iii) Crime ::3:: KL,J & PSS,J wp_9739_2023 No.284/2021 for offences punishable under Section 120-B, 147, 148, 302, 207, 201 r/w Section 149 of I.P.C. and Section 25(1A) of Indian Arms Act, 1959.
However, the said crimes were not relied on by the 2nd respondent while issuing the impugned detention order.
Therefore, the aforesaid three criminal cases are stale cases.

It is relevant to note that, though there are serious allegations against the detenu in the aforesaid crimes, however the detaining authority did not rely upon the same, and there is no explanation forthcoming from the detaining authority on the said aspect.

9. According to learned Special Government Pleader, the Court below, vide order dated 16.08.2022 in Crl.M.P.No.482 of 2022, granted mandatory bail to the detenu on condition that the detenu shall appear before the Station House Officer, Mailardevpally Police Station, Cyberabad between 10:30 a.m. to 04:00 p.m. on every Wednesday till filing of charge-sheet (or) till six (06) weeks, whichever is earlier.

10. Perusal of the record would further reveal that the Investigating Officer, in the aforesaid said three crimes including Crime No.381 of 2022, did not file any application seeking cancellation of bail granted to the detenu on the ground ::4:: KL,J & PSS,J wp_9739_2023 that detenu had committed similar offences and he is not cooperating with the Investigating Officer in concluding the investigation and that the detenu had violated the conditions of bail imposed by the Court below.
Further, the Investigating Officers have also not opposed the bail applications filed by the detenu.

11. As discussed supra, when the detaining authority referred the aforesaid three crimes and the same were not relied on by the detaining authority in the impugned detention order, the detaining authority cannot now rely on the same.
The said principle was laid down by the Honourable Apex Court in Mohinder Singh Gill vs. The Chief Election Commissioner1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The detaining authority cannot improve its version in the counter-affidavit by referring the aforesaid three crimes.
Therefore, we are of the considered opinion that the impugned detention order came to be passed by the 2nd respondent solely relying on a solitary crime, viz., Crime No.381 of 2022.
Further, there is no dispute with regard to legal position that an order of detention can be passed by relying on a solitary crime.

Furthermore, the detaining authority ought to have considered 1978 AIR 851 ::5:: KL,J &
PSS,J wp_9739_2023 the nature of offence and the manner in which the same was committed by the detenu.
Therefore, there is no consideration of the said aspects by the detaining authority while issuing the impugned detention order.
Already, the Investigating Officers have set the criminal law into motion by registering the above solitary crime against the detenu.

12. The Honourable Apex Court and this Court have, time and again, categorically held that detention orders can be passed in rarest of rare cases, that too, to prevent the detenu from Tainiyath Jahan vs The State Of Telangana on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168610832/
2 committing similar offence.

sentences.text: 13. In the present case, the detention order was passed by the 2nd respondent by relying on the solitary crime.
There is no mention in the detention order that the acts of the detenu disturbed the public order.

14. Therefore, in the light of the above discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that the i m p u g n e d d e t e n t i o n o r d e r p a s s e d b y t h e 2 n d r e s p o n d e n t v i d e p r o c e e d i n g s No.07/PD-CELL/CYD/2023, dated 28.01.2023 and also the Confirmation Order passed by 1st respondent vide ::6:: KL,J & PSS,J wp_9739_2023 G.O.Rt.No.420, dated 17.03.2023, are liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, they are set aside.
15. The Writ Petition is allowed.

The respondents are directed to set the detenu, viz., Mohammed Adnan, S/o.Md. Osman, Aged : 24 years, Occ : Driver, R/o.Saifi Colony, Near Nice Hotel, Guntal Shah Baba Dargah, Vattepally, Mailaredevpally, Rajendranagar Mandal, Ranga Reddy District, free forthwith, if he is no longer required in any other criminal case.
No costs.
16. As a sequel, miscellaneous applications pending if any in this Writ Petition, shall stand closed.
